newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen consolidating, watching U.S..
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen consolidating, watching U.S..

text.p: Belgian shares, which suffered light losses on Monday, are expected to stay in a consolidation pattern in the coming days with direction thereafter dependant on the direction of U.S. economic policy, traders said.
"We need a consolidation, a rest for a while," one trader said.

"What happens after that will depend on U.S. economic policy. Even if you accept that there will be no rate rise before the election, there will still be economic indicators that will give us pointers as to what will happen after it," the trader added.
Some other traders were even more bullish, talking of a stabilisation before a fresh rally.
"We will remain in consolidation mode in the coming days. We think it is possible there will then be a strong move upwards," one said. "The risk is on the upside."
However, other traders said the Belgian market strength was based on a combination of the firm dollar and still rising bond prices which would be reversed when interest rates were formally raised.
This in turn would undermine the share market and could trigger a sharp decline, they said.
On Monday the Belgian market was weaker than most of its European counterparts -- a fact that traders wrote off to profittaking after recent gains.
Dollar sensitive stocks like retailer Delhaize which rose 0.3 percent to 1,730 francs, benefitted from the stronger U.S. currency.
Generale Bank, going for a capital increase and facing a new bank tax in Tuesday's 1997 national budget, slipped 75 francs to 10,850.
By contrast Kredietbank, facing the same tax but not looking for new capital, rose 25 francs to 10,300.
The BEL-20 share index ended a day spent entirely in the red with pared losses of 1.98 points or 0.11 percent at 1,771.23 in a 1,771.45/1,764.78 range.
There were 13 losers, two unchanged and five gainers. Total market volume was two billion francs.
